newsitem.title: BULGARIA: U.S. FIRM BUYS BULGARIAN INDUSTRIAL PLANT.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FIRM BUYS BULGARIAN INDUSTRIAL PLANT.

text.p: Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said on Thursday it had sold 77 percent of Sevlievo-based firm Vidima, which produces sanitary and industrial fittings, to U.S. firm American Standard Companies Inc for $5.4 million.
The remaining 23 percent of Vidima will be offered to employees at a preferential price and used to cover property claims by former pre-communist owners, a Privatisation Agency statement said.
New York-based plumbing fixtures maker American Standard has 51 percent in its established joint venture with Vidima, named Vidima Ideal.

Ten percent of the price is to be paid in cash on the day of signing the contract and another 40 percent must be paid within 14 days after the contract is in force. The remainder should be paid with Brady bonds within 60 days after the contract is in force.
Under the deal the new owner pledged to invest $5 million in the plant in the next five years.
Bulgaria plans quick sell-offs of state enterprises this year in a bid to raise desperately needed cash.
